correctness.rationale: From actual RESULT.md, sampling matrices L=(1-t)I+tT and M=tI+(1-t)T yield G=2((1-t)^2+t^2)I+2t(1-t)(T+T^{-1}); its cyclic inverse is the periodization of (-q)^|k|/(2(1-2t)) with q=t/(1-t). Multiplication by L^T,M^T simplifies to two geometric signed rows at a knot; summing absolute coefficients gives (1-q^N)/((1-2t)(1-(-q)^N)). Each cell interior evaluation is an affine mix of adjacent nodal rows, and opposing nonzero sample signs make interior inequality strict. Constant reproduction gives sharp negativity (1-||R||)/2. Odd formula equals coth(u)tanh(Nu), strictly increasing in t and tending to N; at t=1/2 the odd sample map is invertible but even map singular, and t=0 is nodal interpolation. Independently constructed observation matrix and exact-rational Gauss inverse for 21 (N,t) pairs 3<=N<=9, recovering all row total-variation formulas; finite tests supplement the geometric all-N proof.

value.rationale: A sharp L∞ stability constant for a natural symmetric two-sample cell quadrature is a meaningful finite-dimensional operator invariant for numerical splines. Its exact parity dependence, norming-site rigidity, positivity defect and coalescence transition distinguish stable odd midpoint sampling from unstable even cycles and can guide quadrature design; not merely reproducing generic boundedness.

limitations: Only real periodic piecewise-affine splines, equal weights and uniformly spaced symmetric point samples; continuous L2 projections and nonuniform meshes are different operators.
